purpose: Tighten the AP Statistics hand-drawn grading contract so geometry and completeness are structural, labeling is legibility-based, and unable_to_determine is reserved for genuine visual uncertainty.
global_rules: Score only what is visible in the image.
Hand-drawn wobble does not fail geometry unless the intended structure is no longer recoverable.
Labeling is legibility-based; do not require typography-perfect text.
Completeness means the requested structural components are present, including any required marked value, comparison, or estimate.
Use unable_to_determine only when the key structure or label cannot be recovered from the image.

notes: The curve must be recognizable as the requested increasing or decreasing relationship.
If the prompt asks for a marked point or estimate, that mark/value is required for completeness.

criterion_definitions.met_rule: The curve is the correct requested graph family and relationship.
Axis titles and any required marked point/value are legible enough to recover intended meaning.
Curve shape and marked point placement are recoverable despite ordinary hand-drawn wobble.
The curve includes the prompt-specified mark/value and covers the intended range.

notes: The point cloud must be visible, and the trend line should reflect the stated direction.
If the prompt asks for a line of best fit, a visibly reasonable line is required for completeness.

criterion_definitions.met_rule: The response is recognizably a scatterplot for the requested variables.
Axis titles, scale cues, and any title or annotations are legible enough to recover meaning.
Point placement and trend line orientation are consistent with the requested relationship.
All required points and the requested trend line or contextual description are present.

notes: Count accuracy matters more than decorative polish.
A slight spacing wobble is acceptable if the values and counts remain recoverable.

criterion_definitions.met_rule: The response is recognizably a dotplot for the requested data.
The numeric axis and any title or context labels are legible enough to recover the data scale.
Dot counts and placement make the distribution recoverable despite normal hand-drawn wobble.
All data values are represented and the prompt-required shape or outlier note is present if asked.

notes: Treat this as a structural segmented-bar task, not as a requirement for perfect mosaic or pixel-perfect bar geometry.
The key question is whether within-group proportions and category labels are recoverable.

criterion_definitions.met_rule: The response is recognizably a segmented bar display for the requested categories.
Group names, category labels, and a relative-frequency axis or equivalent are legible enough to recover meaning.
Partition lines and segment proportions are recoverable despite hand-drawn wobble.
All requested groups and category segments are present, with the full bar structure visible.

notes: Boxplot geometry should be judged by recoverability of the five-number structure, not by perfect scale precision.
Handwritten labels count if they are legible enough to identify the groups and axis.

criterion_definitions.met_rule: The response is recognizably a side-by-side boxplot comparison for the requested groups.
The axis and group labels are legible enough to identify the compared groups and variable.
The five-number structure and common scale are recoverable despite hand-drawn wobble.
Both groups' boxplots are present and the comparison task is fully represented.
